EXT. RAYAPURAM BUS STAND - DAY
Section: ACT ONE
FADE IN:
Heat shimmer over a row of parked buses. Hawkers call out prices. A loudspeaker announces departures nobody can understand.
A green and cream bus, number plate RYP 0417, swings into the last bay. Painted on its side: RAYAPURAM TO PEDDA REVU, ALL STOPS.
FAROOQ (40s, driver, moustache, sleeves rolled) kills the engine and slaps the steering wheel like a horse's neck.
FAROOQ
Shabash. Two hundred kilometres and not one complaint.
The door hisses open. LAKSHMI (17, backpack, earbuds, a toolkit roll under one arm) steps down and squints at the town.
FAROOQ (CONT'D)
(calling after her)
Hey, engineer! You forgot your umbrella.
He tosses it. She catches it without looking.
LAKSHMI
It hasn't rained here in forty days.
FAROOQ
That is exactly when it rains.
INT. VENKAT RADIO WORKS - DAY
A narrow shop crowded floor to ceiling with radios: valve sets, transistor sets, a ship's receiver the size of a fridge. A ceiling fan turns slowly enough to count.
VENKAT RAO (70s, thick glasses on a string, cotton vest) bends over a workbench, SOLDERING IRON in hand. A thin curl of smoke rises.
Lakshmi stands in the doorway. He does not look up.
VENKAT RAO
If you are a customer, the shop is closed. If you are my granddaughter, you are late.
LAKSHMI
The bus was late.
VENKAT RAO
Farooq's bus is never late. It is only slow.
She drops her bag and hugs him from behind. He keeps soldering.
LAKSHMI
తాతయ్యా, you still have the fridge radio.
VENKAT RAO
It is a marine receiver. Show some respect.
He sets the iron in its stand and finally looks at her.
VENKAT RAO (CONT'D)
You grew. Did they teach you anything at that college?
LAKSHMI
Signals and systems. Mostly systems.
VENKAT RAO
Then you can hold this.
He hands her a MULTIMETER and points at two terminals.
EXT. VENKAT RADIO WORKS - ROOFTOP - DUSK
The town spreads out in orange light. A rusted ANTENNA MAST leans against the water tank, guy wires slack.
Lakshmi climbs onto the parapet. Venkat Rao stays by the stairs, holding a cup of tea.
VENKAT RAO
Come down. That mast is older than your mother.
LAKSHMI
Why is it still up here?
VENKAT RAO
Because nobody asked me to take it down.
She runs a hand along a guy wire. It sings faintly in the breeze.
INT. VENKAT RAO'S HOUSE - KITCHEN - NIGHT
A small kitchen. Steel plates, rice, a pot of rasam. On the shelf, a TRANSISTOR RADIO with a cracked case, held together with tape.
The radio crackles. A NEWSREADER (V.O.) speaks through static.
NEWSREADER (V.O.)
...a deep depression over the Bay is likely to intensify. Fishermen are advised not to venture out...
Venkat Rao reaches over and turns the volume up.
LAKSHMI
It will turn north. They always turn north.
VENKAT RAO
They always turn north until one does not.
He eats in silence. Then:
VENKAT RAO (CONT'D)
Pedda Revu had a station once. Community radio. I built the transmitter in 1989.
LAKSHMI
What happened to it?
VENKAT RAO
Phones happened. Everybody stopped listening.
INT. DISTRICT OFFICE - CORRIDOR - DAY
A long corridor with green walls and files stacked on benches. A wall clock runs four minutes slow.
Lakshmi and Venkat Rao wait on a bench. Venkat Rao holds a cloth bag against his chest.
SURESH (30s, district clerk, pen behind each ear) hurries past, stops, comes back.
SURESH
Venkat garu? From the radio shop?
VENKAT RAO
From the radio shop.
SURESH
Come, come. Sit at my desk. It has a fan.
INT. DISTRICT OFFICE - SURESH'S DESK - CONTINUOUS
A desk buried in paper. A PEDESTAL FAN turns its head left and right as if refusing everything.
Venkat Rao opens the cloth bag and lays out an old LEDGER with a cracked spine. Hand-ruled columns. Dates, frequencies, call signs.
VENKAT RAO
The Pedda Revu licence. The station is still on your list.
Suresh turns pages, puzzled.
SURESH
Sir, this tower was decommissioned on paper in 2011.
LAKSHMI
On paper. Is it still standing?
SURESH
(beat)
Nobody has gone to check.
He looks at the window. The sky outside has gone a strange yellow.
EXT. RAYAPURAM MARKET - DAY
Crowded stalls. Steel vessels, chillies in heaps, plastic buckets in every colour.
PADMA (50s, sharp eyes, a basket of dried fish on her hip) argues with a VENDOR over a coil of rope.
Lakshmi and Venkat Rao pass. Padma sees Venkat Rao and stops mid-sentence.
PADMA
Radio Venkat! You are alive!
VENKAT RAO
So are you, Padma. Still shouting.
PADMA
If I whisper, nobody in Pedda Revu hears anything. Your tower is dead. The phones die whenever the wind blows. Last monsoon we heard about the warning after the water came.
Lakshmi looks at her grandfather. He looks at the ledger in his bag.
INT. VENKAT RADIO WORKS - NIGHT
The shop lit by a single bulb. Lakshmi sits cross-legged on the floor with the ledger open. Venkat Rao pulls a dusty crate from under the bench.
Inside: VALVES wrapped in newspaper, a coil of COPPER WIRE, a TRANSFORMER with a handwritten tag: "PEDDA REVU SPARE."
LAKSHMI
You kept spares for thirty years.
VENKAT RAO
I kept spares because nobody asked me to throw them away.
LAKSHMI
We could go. Just to look.
VENKAT RAO
(not looking up)
Farooq leaves at six.
Company move: the unit leaves Rayapuram after this scene and shoots everything from scene 13 onward on the coast. Plan a travel day.
EXT. RAYAPURAM BUS STAND - DAWN
Grey light. The bus idles in its bay, engine coughing.
Lakshmi carries the crate. Venkat Rao carries the transformer like a newborn. Farooq leans out of the driver's window.
FAROOQ
Arre, यह radio तो museum में होना चाहिए!
VENKAT RAO
The museum is where I am going.
Farooq laughs and pops the luggage hatch.
INT. FAROOQ'S BUS - MOVING - DAY
The bus rattles through paddy fields. Every window is open. A goat stands in the aisle, its owner asleep.
Lakshmi sits behind the driver, ledger open on her knees. Farooq watches her in the mirror.
FAROOQ
What is in the book?
LAKSHMI
Frequencies. Who was on air, when, for how long.
FAROOQ
My father had a show. Every Sunday. Film songs and fish prices.
LAKSHMI
(finding the page)
"Sunday, 0700. Farooq senior. Songs and prices."
Farooq goes quiet. He drives.
FAROOQ
चिंता मत करो, बस पहुँच जाएगी। Every time.
EXT. COASTAL HIGHWAY - DAY
A straight road between casuarina trees. The wind pushes the trees all one way.
The bus slows. Ahead, a POLICE JEEP is parked across the road, light bar flashing. Plastic barriers.
EXT. COASTAL HIGHWAY - CHECKPOST - DAY
CONSTABLE RAJU (20s, oversized raincoat, whistle) waves the bus down. Farooq leans out.
CONSTABLE RAJU
रास्ता बंद है। Cyclone warning.
FAROOQ
Bhai, I have passengers for Pedda Revu. They live there.
CONSTABLE RAJU
Then they should be leaving Pedda Revu, not going.
Lakshmi climbs down from the bus with the ledger.
LAKSHMI
There is no warning reaching the village. No signal. If we fix the tower, they can hear the district office.
Constable Raju looks at the girl, the old man in the window, the crate.
CONSTABLE RAJU
(sighing)
You have until the evening. After that I am not coming to rescue a radio.
He drags one barrier aside.
Section: ACT TWO
EXT. PEDDA REVU - BEACH - DAY
Wide flat sand. A row of FISHING BOATS pulled high above the tide line, painted blue and red. Nets drying on poles.
The bus stops at the end of the road. Children run alongside it. BITTU (10, too-big cricket cap) runs fastest.
BITTU
Bus! Bus! Padma akka, the bus brought a grandfather!
Padma comes out of a hut, wiping her hands.
PADMA
He brought himself. The bus only helped.
EXT. PEDDA REVU - COMMUNITY RADIO HUT - DAY
A whitewashed hut on a low rise above the village, its paint gone grey. Beside it, a lattice STEEL TOWER, forty metres high, red and white bands faded to pink and cream.
Venkat Rao stops at the bottom of the slope. He looks up at the tower for a long moment.
VENKAT RAO
She is still standing.
LAKSHMI
Is that good?
VENKAT RAO
Ask me tonight.
INT. COMMUNITY RADIO HUT - DAY
Dust in slanting light. A bird's nest on the mixing desk. Posters for health camps from twenty years ago.
In the corner, the TRANSMITTER: a grey steel cabinet with dials and a brass plate that reads "BUILT BY V. RAO, 1989."
Lakshmi wipes the plate with her sleeve. Venkat Rao pretends not to see.
LAKSHMI
You signed it.
VENKAT RAO
Every good engineer signs his work. Then he cannot blame anyone else.
He opens the cabinet. Spiders scatter.
EXT. PADMA'S HOUSE - VERANDA - NIGHT
A kerosene LANTERN on the floor. Padma serves rice and fish curry on banana leaves. Bittu eats with both hands. Farooq has joined them.
Padma holds up her phone. No bars.
PADMA
ఇక్కడ ఫోన్ సిగ్నల్ రాదు. When the wind comes, nothing comes.
FAROOQ
And the radio?
PADMA
The radio was Venkat's. When he stopped coming, the radio stopped talking.
Venkat Rao puts down his food.
VENKAT RAO
I stopped coming because nobody listened.
PADMA
(gently)
We listened. We just did not tell you.
INT. COMMUNITY RADIO HUT - NIGHT
Lantern light. Lakshmi and Venkat Rao work side by side. She tests valves with the multimeter. He sorts them into good and bad piles on a newspaper.
LAKSHMI
Seven good. Three dead.
VENKAT RAO
Seven is enough. Seven is always enough.
Outside, the wind finds a gap in the roof and moans.
EXT. PEDDA REVU - BEACH - NIGHT
Bittu and two other CHILDREN sit on an upturned boat watching the sea. The waves are higher than usual and very loud.
BITTU
My father says the sea is angry.
CHILD
The sea is not angry. It is just big.
A wave runs further up the sand than any before it. The children pull their feet up.
INT. FAROOQ'S BUS - PARKED - NIGHT
Farooq lies across the back seat, a towel over his eyes. A small battery RADIO on his chest plays only static.
He turns the dial slowly. Static. Static. A fragment of the district news, gone again.
FAROOQ
(to the radio)
Come on. You did it for my father.
EXT. COMMUNITY RADIO HUT - TOWER BASE - DAY
Morning. Grey clouds racing. Lakshmi straps on an old CLIMBING HARNESS from the hut. Venkat Rao holds a coil of ANTENNA WIRE and will not let go of it.
VENKAT RAO
The feeder is broken at the top. I will go.
LAKSHMI
Thatha, you get dizzy on a chair.
VENKAT RAO
I got dizzy on that chair once.
LAKSHMI
Twice. Amma told me.
He hands her the wire. His hands shake slightly.
VENKAT RAO
నెమ్మదిగా. Slowly. Clip in at every section.
EXT. TOWER - TOP - DAY
Wind. The whole tower hums. Lakshmi clips in, one rung, then the next. Far below, the village is small and the sea is enormous.
ANGLE ON THE BROKEN FEEDER
A frayed cable flaps against the steel. Lakshmi grabs it, strips the end with her teeth, twists it onto the new wire, tapes it.
LAKSHMI
(shouting down)
Done!
From below, faintly:
VENKAT RAO (O.S.)
Do not say done until it works!
INT. COMMUNITY RADIO HUT - DAY
Venkat Rao throws the main switch. The transmitter hums. The dials rise. A smell of hot dust.
Then a CRACK and a puff of smoke. The dials drop to zero.
Lakshmi pulls the panel. The old TRANSFORMER is black and split.
LAKSHMI
Thatha, this transformer is gone. పూర్తిగా కాలిపోయింది.
VENKAT RAO
Then we use the spare.
LAKSHMI
The spare needs a battery bank. We have no battery bank.
Farooq appears in the doorway, out of breath.
FAROOQ
The boats have batteries. Big ones. For the lights.
EXT. PEDDA REVU - FISHING BOAT - DAY
Padma's boat, LAKSHMI DEVI painted on the bow in curling letters. Padma unscrews a heavy MARINE BATTERY from under the deck boards.
PADMA
My husband named this boat after a goddess. Not after you.
LAKSHMI
I know.
PADMA
So bring the battery back.
Farooq and Lakshmi lift it together. Bittu carries the cables like a crown.
INT. COMMUNITY RADIO HUT - DUSK
The spare transformer wired in. The battery on the floor, clamps attached. Lakshmi checks every joint with the lantern.
Venkat Rao sits down heavily on an upturned crate. He presses a hand to his chest.
LAKSHMI
Thatha?
VENKAT RAO
I am fine. It is the heat.
LAKSHMI
It is not hot.
He tries to stand. He does not manage it.
INT. PRIMARY HEALTH CENTRE - NIGHT
A two-bed clinic with a single generator light. Rain begins against the window.
DR. KAVITHA NAIR (40s, calm, reading glasses on her head) takes Venkat Rao's blood pressure. Lakshmi stands at the foot of the bed.
DR. KAVITHA NAIR
His heart is tired. Not broken. He needs to lie still until morning.
VENKAT RAO
The storm will not lie still until morning.
DR. KAVITHA NAIR
Then somebody else will have to talk to it.
Venkat Rao looks at Lakshmi. He takes the ledger from the bedside table and holds it out.
VENKAT RAO
Frequency is on page one. My handwriting. Speak slowly. Say where to go and say it twice.
She takes the book.
LAKSHMI
తాతయ్యా, తుఫాను వస్తోంది.
VENKAT RAO
భయపడకు, అమ్మా. ఈ రేడియో ఇంకా బతికే ఉంది.
Section: ACT THREE
EXT. PEDDA REVU - VILLAGE LANE - NIGHT
Rain sideways. Palm fronds tear loose and skid down the lane. A dog runs past with nowhere to go.
Lakshmi runs uphill toward the hut, the ledger zipped inside her jacket.
INT. COMMUNITY RADIO HUT - NIGHT
Water drips through the roof onto the mixing desk. Lakshmi throws a plastic sheet over it. She flips the main switch.
The transmitter hums. The dials rise and hold.
She pulls the MICROPHONE toward her. Her hands are shaking. She opens the ledger to page one, reads the frequency, sets the dial.
She keys the microphone.
LAKSHMI
(into the microphone)
This is Pedda Revu community radio. Testing. Testing.
Nothing comes back. She swallows.
LAKSHMI (CONT'D)
(slowly, clearly)
పెద్ద రేవు ప్రజలారా, అందరూ బడికి వెళ్ళండి. అక్కడ సురక్షితం.
(beat)
Everyone in Pedda Revu, go to the school. It is safe there. I will say it again.
INT. DISTRICT OFFICE - CONTROL ROOM - NIGHT
A room of radios and one tired computer. Suresh, sleeves rolled up, drinks tea from a paper cup. A RECEIVER on the shelf crackles to life.
LAKSHMI (V.O.)
...go to the school. It is safe there...
Suresh drops the cup. He grabs the desk phone.
SURESH
(into phone)
Sir, Pedda Revu is on air. Yes. The old station. Yes, sir, the one on paper.
EXT. PEDDA REVU - VILLAGE LANE - NIGHT - INTERCUT
INTERCUT between the radio hut and the lane.
Doors open. In one house a small radio plays Lakshmi's voice. In another, an old man holds a set to his ear.
Padma steps into the rain with a torch and starts banging on doors.
PADMA
Did you hear? The school! Everybody to the school!
In the hut, Lakshmi keeps talking.
LAKSHMI
(into the microphone)
Take water. Take medicines. Leave the boats. The boats will wait.
INT. PEDDA REVU SCHOOL - NIGHT
A single-storey school on high ground. Families crowd into classrooms. Mats on the floor. A teacher counts heads with a chalk tally on the blackboard.
Bittu sits by the window holding a radio. Lakshmi's voice comes through, steady now.
BITTU
That is Lakshmi akka. She climbed the tower.
DR. KAVITHA NAIR enters, wheeling Venkat Rao in a plastic chair fitted with bicycle wheels. He is wrapped in a blanket and smiling.
VENKAT RAO
Turn it up. She is doing it properly.
INT. COMMUNITY RADIO HUT - NIGHT
The tower creaks outside. A gust hits. The hut door bangs open and rain pours in.
The battery clamp sparks. The dials dip. Lakshmi jams a pencil against the clamp to hold it and keeps talking.
LAKSHMI
(into the microphone)
If you are on the beach road, do not walk. Wait. Someone is coming.
She looks at the door. Nobody is coming.
Then: HEADLIGHTS through the rain. A horn, long and loud.
EXT. PEDDA REVU - VILLAGE LANE - NIGHT
Farooq's BUS crawls up the lane, wipers useless, headlights full. Water up to the hubcaps.
Farooq hangs out of the window, shouting.
FAROOQ
Beach road! Anyone on the beach road!
Figures appear in the headlights. A woman with a child. Two old men holding each other up. They climb aboard.
FAROOQ (CONT'D)
(to himself)
मैं गाड़ी लेकर आता हूँ। Every time.
He reverses the bus all the way up the hill to the school, horn blaring.
EXT. PEDDA REVU - BEACH - DAWN
Silence after the storm. The sand is covered in branches and broken planks. Two boats lie on their sides. The rest are whole.
Villagers walk down from the school in a slow line. Padma checks her boat and pats its bow.
PADMA
Still a goddess.
Above the village the tower stands, a little crooked, red and white against a clean sky.
INT. COMMUNITY RADIO HUT - DAY
Sunlight through the holes in the roof. Lakshmi sleeps at the desk, head on her arms, headphones still on.
Venkat Rao, walking now with a stick, lays the ledger beside her. He uncaps a pen.
INSERT - THE LEDGER
A new line in the columns, in his careful hand: "Monday, 2140 to 0510. Lakshmi. Everyone went to the school."
BACK TO SCENE
He blows on the ink so it will dry. He does not wake her.
EXT. COASTAL HIGHWAY - DAY
The bus heads back toward Rayapuram. The barriers are gone. Constable Raju waves from his jeep, his raincoat torn.
INT. FAROOQ'S BUS - MOVING - CONTINUOUS
Lakshmi and Venkat Rao sit behind the driver. Farooq's battery radio is on the dashboard, tuned to the Pedda Revu frequency. Padma's voice reads out the fish prices.
FAROOQ
Next Sunday, film songs. My slot.
LAKSHMI
Thatha, you never gave him the slot.
VENKAT RAO
His father had it. Now he has it.
He closes his eyes and listens.
FADE OUT.
THE END
